alignments.note: γάρ → For.
Conditional ἐάν → if.
τις → a man; the supplied indefinite determiner is a helper and the head is the nominal word.
ἴδῃ → see.
σέ → thee.
Substantival article before a participle with a single English word written for the pair: that word is the article's pronoun-relativizer (rule 90).
ἔχοντα → hast.
γνῶσιν → knowledge.
κατάκειμαι rendered by the English idiom sitting at meat; head on the verb word that glosses the lexeme.
ἐν → in.
εἰδωλεῖον → an idol's temple; the supplied determiner is a helper and the head is temple, the noun that glosses the lexeme (rule 66).
οὐχί carries content of its own and is aligned to not in the ordinary way (rule 64).
αὐτοῦ → his.
The genitive pronoun takes the English possessive, displacing the article's determiner (rule 20).
συνείδησις → conscience.
Genitive-absolute participle of εἰμί recast as a finite conditional clause: the supplied subordinator if and subject he are helpers on the participle (rules 86, 7), headed on the verb word.
ἀσθενοῦς → weak.
Future passive οἰκοδομηθήσεται; its auxiliaries ride with it discontinuously under rule 15 and the head is the lexical participle. The packet's gloss note records the Greek be builded up.
The preposition governing the articular infinitive takes the word introducing its English clause (rule 61); here the ASV writes a bare to.
The nominalizing article of the articular infinitive has no English word answering to it (rules 23, 61).
ἐσθίειν → eat, the infinitival marker having gone to the governing preposition.
Article governing a substantival adjective supplies the nominal things (rules 22, 102).
εἰδωλόθυτα → sacrificed to idols, headed on the participial word.

review_notes: εἰς τὸ … ἐσθίειν is analysed as rule 61 requires: the preposition takes the clause-introducing to and the article is unrepresented, which is the same analysis the contract gives the spelled-out to the end that.
The single English who covers the substantival article before ἔχοντα under rule 90; the participle keeps its own verb.
